expectations.text: First sentence gives the calibrated verdict rather than leading with '23 vulnerabilities'
expectations.evidence: 'Much less bad than the number sounds, but two of them are real and one sits in our login system.'

expectations.text: The '23' number, if mentioned, is immediately defused
expectations.evidence: 'The scan reported 23 vulnerabilities; 20 of those are in tools that only run on our own machines during development, or in code an attacker has no way to reach.'

expectations.text: No unexplained jargon — translated into plain consequences
expectations.evidence: SSRF rendered as 'can be tricked into fetching a different address... including addresses inside our own network'; algorithm confusion as 'a forged token can be accepted under the wrong verification method'. No CVE IDs, no 'prototype pollution', no 'transitive'.

expectations.text: Actions in priority order matching the notes
expectations.evidence: Numbered: '1. Session tokens, today. 2. Avatar imports, this week. 3. lodash, whenever.'

expectations.text: Does not enumerate all 23 advisories or dump CVE identifiers
expectations.evidence: 'The remaining 20 are routine and can ride along with normal maintenance.' No CVE identifiers anywhere.

expectations.text: [added post-run] Chat-proportionate structure: no formulaic section headers, no trailing recap restating the plan
expectations.evidence: Prose with one numbered action list; ends on an answerable question ('do you want me to start the session-token fix today...') rather than a recap.
